project: NJ PBS / New Jersey by the Numbers — verified-source dashboard, October 20 source review
status: published on NJ PBS; source-verified snapshot
notes: Property tax average derived from DCA yearly tables and corroborated by Rutgers reporting; validate the exact source spreadsheet cell during ingestion.
Not all datasets have fixed release days. nextCheck is an internal review reminder, not a guaranteed release date.
No automatic publication. Source changes should create review candidates; an editor approves or overrides.
Property tax historical benchmarks are selected published years only (not a full year-by-year interpolation). Annual minimum-wage history excludes the announced future rate.
A future implementation must compute comparison deltas from the same approved source series and revision. Browser-only overrides invalidate historical comparisons until separately reviewed.
New additions use authoritative government figures; most lack a fully verified historical series, so available snapshot comparisons differ by dataset.
Geographic view is allowed only where all 21 counties (or all 564 municipalities) are enumerated and reconciled; the voter registration panel is the only county view enabled here.
ACS 1-year and ACS 5-year estimates must not be spliced into a time series. Margins of error are shown with median estimates.
Figures and downloads preserve their dated source snapshot; this page does not provide a public API or CMS figure picker.
Chart honesty: bars used to compare absolute totals start at zero. A focused range may never be used to exaggerate changes in population-size counts.
A data release from 2024 or earlier is always dated explicitly; period comparison labels such as one year ago are reserved for current 2025–2026 observations.
A single survey estimate is not depicted as a change or a multi-period trend. If statistical margins are shown, they are numerically described rather than positioned on a misleading magnitude axis.
Voter registration is a count with year-over-year and month-over-month percentage changes. There is intentionally no magnitude chart for 6.6–6.7 million counts.

Source: U.S. Census Bureau Building Permits Survey state monthly series NJBPPRIV, via FRED (October 27, 2026 vintage). Preliminary, not seasonally adjusted. January–September 2026 includes 22,517 privately owned housing units authorized; the same nine months of 2025 include 23,695. Difference −1,178 units (−4.97%). Data are units authorized, not permit documents, starts, completions or individual dwellings occupied. Both totals add only the monthly readings of this single series. Official annual and separately published county year-to-date aggregates have different vintages and must not be combined with these totals.
A 2024 or 2025 figure is explicitly marked as the latest verified period in this source snapshot; it is not represented as a current 2026 condition.

National comparisons appear only for matching units, populations, geography definitions and time windows, from the same federal series/agency. Where no equivalent benchmark is available, state the reason and retain dated internal context.
Percent changes in absolute counts are presented as figures, not truncated-scale magnitude charts. The complete voter-registration table is visible by default for all 21 counties.

November 19 NJDOL October labor update: NJ seasonally adjusted October unemployment 4.2% (unchanged), payroll jobs −900 to 4,379,000; September payroll gain revised from +14,900 to +17,400. CES industry jobs are not occupations or unique people. Historical unemployment through September retains the October 20 BLS snapshot; preliminary October appended from NJDOL. October 2025 unemployment is missing, not zero.

No verified monthly occupational job-gains series exists in the NJDOL September 2026 release. Occupations are different from industries; the wage survey OEWS is not monthly and is excluded rather than inferred.

Three unpopulated/reuse-unresolved dataset panels excluded from this collection: occupation mean wages (unverified value), NJ TRANSIT performance (data reuse not cleared), and 2025 goods exports (official source conflict). These are not displayed, exported or replicated.

Rutgers nClimDiv statewide monthly table updated through October 2026, verified November 9. September and other months were revised. The source values for 2026, same months of 2025 and the 1991–2020 normals are taken from one identical revised table and compared only over January–October.

The temperature figure uses the November 9, 2026 Rutgers nClimDiv statewide mean-temperature table through October, including revised July–September readings. Temperature and precipitation are separate elements; each must use its own matching observed months and 1991–2020 normals from a single revision.

BLS CPI-U September 2026 report published October 14: 4.5% annual inflation for NY–NJ–PA metro versus 3.7% for U.S. CPI-U in same report month. No NJ statewide CPI-U exists in these BLS metro results.

Published metrics must be status verified, contain a finite numeric value, and link to a primary official public source. Local browser drafts cannot replace the verified public preview. Underlying reuses are still subject to editorial source and terms review.

October 20 source corrections: unemployment history reconciled to one BLS LAUS snapshot; graduation comparison uses the 2021 and 2025 state cohort tables; absence comparisons disclose the 2024–25 inclusion-rule change; SNAP uses the July 2026 DFD report. Publication approval remains separate.

metrics.methodNote: The Census Bureau's ACSBR-028 Appendix Table 1 provides 2025 median household income and 90% margins of error for NJ ($107,797 ±$1,374), the United States ($84,780 ±$215), NY ($89,210 ±$934) and PA ($81,473 ±$603). The default shows NJ 7.7% (±0.3 pp) versus U.S. 8.4% (±0.1 pp); optional age groups show NJ working-age adults 11.1% (±0.4 pp) and children under 19 4.2% (±0.5 pp). All margins are 90% margins of error. The 2025 questionnaire and processing were changed; pre-2025 health-insurance estimates are not treated as a directly comparable time series.
metrics.title: Residents without health insurance
metrics.description: Share of New Jersey's civilian noninstitutionalized population without comprehensive health insurance in 2025; 2025 American Community Survey 1-year estimates.
metrics.insight: In 2025, 7.7% of New Jersey residents in the ACS civilian noninstitutionalized population were uninsured versus 8.4% nationally. Among New Jersey residents, the uninsured rate was 11.1% for adults ages 19–64 and 4.2% for children under 19.
metrics.source: U.S. Census Bureau, Health Insurance Coverage by State: 2025 (ACSBR-027), Appendix Table A-2

metrics.methodNote: Census Bureau ACSBR-027, Appendix Table A-2, October 2026, 2025 American Community Survey (ACS) 1-year. Universe: civilian noninstitutionalized population. Uninsured means no comprehensive health insurance at time of interview, including people whose only coverage was through Indian Health Service. Survey estimates describe the annual average of coverage status at the time of interview, not Medicaid/NJ FamilyCare administrative enrollments. All chart values from one source table and estimate year. Margins of error (± percentage points) represent 90% confidence intervals. The NJ−U.S. difference of −0.7 percentage point is the arithmetic difference of two rounded rates, not a confidence interval for the difference; no unsupported significance claim. Age rates have age-specific denominators and do not represent shares of all uninsured people. The 2025 ACS changed questions and processing, and the Census cautions that comparisons with 2024 and earlier estimates may be misleading.

metrics.chartTitle: New Jersey four-year graduation-rate change since class of 2022
metrics.historyChartNote: Default chart uses percentage-point changes since class of 2022, for NJDOE's state-calculated four-year adjusted cohorts 2022 (90.9%), 2023 (91.1%), 2024 (91.3%), and 2025 (91.8%). Its zero line represents no change since 2022, not zero graduates. The student-group toggle uses class-of-2025 four-year state rates (statewide 91.8%, economically disadvantaged 88.9%, students with disabilities 82.4%) from NJDOE's 2025 official cohort report. Group memberships may overlap and rates are not additive. Federal calculation and five/six-year cohorts are excluded. The 2021 state four-year rate is 90.6%, as independently confirmed in NJDOE's 2024 state-version chart; a May 2026 press release describes 90.9% as a four-years-earlier baseline, apparently referring to the 2022 value. The chart starts at 2022 until that editorial conflict is explicitly annotated.

metrics.period: Class of 2025 · state four-year adjusted cohort

metrics.source: NJ Department of Education, state-calculated four-year adjusted cohort graduation data, classes of 2022–2025

metrics.methodNote: Authoritative NJDOE 2025 four-year adjusted cohort archive includes the 2022–2025 state version rates in the same multi-cohort workbook, and class of 2025 student-group rates from the corresponding year cohort workbook. State calculation counts all students earning state-endorsed diplomas; the federal calculation excludes certain graduates under ESSA criteria. Cohorts have different graduating populations; these are cohort rates, not a panel of students followed across cohorts. In the four-year state-version series, 2022 90.9%, 2023 91.1%, 2024 91.3%, 2025 91.8%; gain +0.9 percentage point since 2022 and +0.5 from 2024. The 2021 state four-year rate was 90.6% according to NJDOE's 2024 State Board chart and 2021 cohort table; the May 7, 2026 summary's attribution of 90.9% to four years prior conflicts with those records. The 2025 student-group rates 88.9% economically disadvantaged and 82.4% disabilities use the 2025 state cohort methodology and do not sum to or partition the statewide rate. Do not mix 4-year and 5-year rates, state and federal calculations, or treat any delta as a percentage change.
metrics.historySource: NJDOE four-year adjusted cohort graduation rates, state version (2022–2025)

metrics.chartTitle: Year-over-year change in NJ SNAP participation, January–July 2026
metrics.historyChartNote: Seven comparable same-month pairs (January–July 2025 and 2026) from DFD's July 2026 Current Program Statistics Table 5. Each bar shows (2026 recipients − 2025 recipients) / 2025 recipients × 100, with zero as no year-over-year change. The 2025 and 2026 participant totals are people receiving SNAP issuances during each reporting month, not household or benefit-dollar totals. The policy timeline is separately sourced and not a statistical causal model.
metrics.title: People receiving NJ SNAP
metrics.description: New Jersey residents who received SNAP benefits during July 2026, with January–July 2026 compared with the same 2025 months from one DFD administrative issuance series.
metrics.insight: In July 2026, 737,447 people received NJ SNAP benefits, 55,669 fewer (−7.0%) than in July 2025. Every available January–July 2026 month had fewer participants than the same month in 2025.
metrics.source: New Jersey Department of Human Services, Division of Family Development, Current Program Statistics, July 2026, Table 5

metrics.methodNote: The New Jersey Division of Family Development's July 2026 Current Program Statistics, Table 5, supplies all 14 2025 and 2026 monthly person-participation observations used here. DFD defines them as households and persons receiving SNAP issuances during each month, derived from NJ MMIS Shared Data Warehouse issuance files. January–July 2026 is compared only with the matching months in 2025. July 2025: 793,116 people; July 2026: 737,447; difference −55,669 (−7.0% of July 2025). This metric excludes SNAP households, eligibility estimates, applications, food insecurity and benefits paid. Separate federal policy milestones are sourced to the NJ DFD Federal Changes to SNAP page and are not causal claims; administrative time series alone cannot attribute the decline to specific laws or implementation dates. Do not mix federal USDA program data with state DFD participation counts.
